# planteam

`planteam` is an R package for annual SAFE/Plan Team summary tables, off-cycle
catch reports, and AKRO specification tables. The existing R Markdown templates
and package API remain available. The new checkout workflow renders a catch
report from an explicit local CSV snapshot to **HTML and Word**, without Google
authentication or installing the full package. It performs no stock assessment,
projection, apportionment, or total calculations.

## Local document-builder app

For the BSAI/GOA SAFE introduction editor, double-click `Start Builder.command`
and open <http://127.0.0.1:3847>. The on-demand Mac service stays available after
the task or launcher terminal closes. Use `Stop Builder.command` when finished.
See [builder setup, editing, saving and rendering](BUILDER.md) and
[the four inspected PDF examples](PDF-EXAMPLES.md). The app keeps both FMPs in a
portable JSON working file and renders HTML, Word and PDF. Its stock-specific
boilerplate contains TODO prompts, with no historical advice presented as current.

## Quick start with synthetic example data

Install [Quarto CLI](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and R (the new scripts
require R >= 4.1; the package's older minimum is unchanged). From this checkout:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla -e 'install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown", "yaml"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'
quarto check knitr
Rscript --vanilla scripts/test-report.R
Rscript --vanilla scripts/render-report.R --example
```

Open `_output/example/catch-report.html` or
`_output/example/catch-report.docx`. Both visibly label the invented example.
The CSV contains invented values; it is neither historical evidence nor advice.
The Quarto R package, LaTeX, Google credentials, and the `planteam` package are
unnecessary for this path. Install packages once; subsequent renders are offline.

## Render approved production data

```sh
mkdir -p inputs
cp config/catch-report.production.example.yml inputs/catch-report.yml
# Place an approved snapshot at inputs/specs.csv and fill every YAML null.
Rscript --vanilla scripts/render-report.R --params inputs/catch-report.yml
```

Run from the repository root. Input paths in YAML are root-relative or absolute,
including when the YAML itself is elsewhere. Use a UTF-8, comma-delimited CSV
with a header and one row per `stock,year,area`:

| Required field | Format and meaning |
|---|---|
| `stock` | Lowercase repository shorthand, e.g. `pollock`, `pcod`, `orox`; not a common-name label. `species` is accepted as an alias only when it contains this shorthand. Conflicting aliases fail. |
| `year` | Integer calendar year. Selected rows must cover report year − 1 through year + 2. |
| `area` | Exact management-area label. `GOA` selects `Total`/`GOA-wide`; `BSAI` retains all areas for that stock; other values (e.g. `Bogoslof`) select an exact area. Only the two region selectors are case-insensitive. |
| `ofl`, `abc`, `tac`, `catch` | Nonnegative numeric metric tonnes (t), without thousands separators, formulas or unit strings. Blank or `NA` represents unavailable data; zero remains zero. |

Extra columns are ignored by the catch report. No units are inferred or converted.
Missing files/columns, duplicate keys, malformed numbers, empty selections,
incomplete year coverage and invalid metadata stop the render. Production mode
refuses the bundled `examples/` path; there is no automatic fallback. An analyst
must confirm units, the source revision, assessment schedule and approval status.

The parameter YAML requires `example: false`, `doc_title`, `authors`, `stock`,
`area`, `year`, `last_full_year`, `next_full_year`, `catch_data_date`, `input_csv`,
`input_source` (source/tab/revision/approval identifier), and a quoted ISO
`snapshot_date`. The previous full assessment must precede the report year and
the next full assessment must follow it. Dates and assessment schedules are
supplied metadata, not verified management decisions.

## Outputs and provenance

The runner writes these exact files under `_output/example/` for `--example`,
or `_output/production/` for `--params`:

- `catch-report.html`: self-contained review document.
- `catch-report.docx`: editable Word document using `inst/template.docx`.
- `catch-table.csv`: selected stock/year/area and supplied numeric values, preserving row order and NA.
- `provenance.yml`: parameters, input/parameter/source/output MD5 identifiers, Git revision and dirty status, UTC render time, R/Quarto/package versions.
- `session-info.txt`: R session details.

Repeated runs overwrite that mode's outputs. Copy an approved bundle to an
access-controlled archive before the next run; retain the input snapshot and
source revision there. A successful bundle has `provenance.yml`; a failed render
can leave partial or older documents and never certifies them. MD5 identifies
content; it is not a security signature. Software versions are recorded rather
than locked. The original `docs/` pkgdown site is unchanged.

For direct Quarto use (documents only, without the CSV/manifest/session bundle):

```sh
quarto render catch-report.qmd --to all --execute-params examples/catch-report.yml --output-dir _output/example
```

`quarto render` without parameters intentionally fails; production inputs are
never guessed. `_quarto.yml` renders only `catch-report.qmd`, so legacy vignettes,
README and live Google Sheet templates are not accidentally executed.

## Existing products and migration

See [workflow evaluation and legacy input/output contracts](WORKFLOW.md) and
[validation evidence and remaining checks](VALIDATION.md). Summary templates,
`catch_report()`, `read_specs()`, `spec_table()`, and `catch_to_sheet()` are
unchanged. The new Quarto workflow runs from a clone, not an installed package.
Full GOA/BSAI summaries and specification exports still use the legacy workflow;
they have not been certified by the example catch-report test.

To install the existing package with all its declared dependencies:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_local(".", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = FALSE)
# Or install upstream main (which omits this feature branch):
# remotes::install_github("afsc-assessments/planteam")
```

## Troubleshooting and restricted inputs

| Symptom | Action |
|---|---|
| `quarto` unavailable | Install the CLI, restart the shell and run `quarto --version`. The R package alone does not install the CLI. |
| Missing R package | Install `knitr`, `rmarkdown`, `yaml` into the R library used by `quarto check knitr`. Set `QUARTO_R` to the intended R installation if needed. |
| Missing input or metadata | Fill `inputs/catch-report.yml` and supply the approved CSV. Never rename example data as production. |
| No rows / missing years | Check shorthand, exact area labels and report year. Include explicit NA rows for unavailable future values; obtain missing source records rather than inventing values. |
| Numeric/schema error | Export values rather than spreadsheet formulas; remove thousands separators, retain missingness and resolve duplicate keys at source. |
| Legacy login or Sheet failure | An authorized analyst must authenticate separately; rendering the new workflow never requests access. No production snapshot was retrieved during this migration. |
| Word differs across machines | HTML is the primary review view; inspect Word in the target editor. The inherited reference DOCX can affect pagination. |

`inputs/`, `_output/`, and `.quarto/` are Git-ignored. A `.gitignore` is not access
control: keep confidential or restricted data on approved storage, do not commit
credentials, and review rendered tables and provenance before sharing. The
manifest includes input paths and source identifiers. Do not upload restricted
snapshots or their derived reports to GitHub, the wiki, or a public document.

The [existing package articles](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/planteam/)
describe the original workflow. To regenerate this README, edit `README.Rmd` and
run `Rscript --vanilla -e 'rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd")'`.
